title: De motu vibratorio laminarum elasticarum, ubi plures novae vibrationum species hactenus non pertractatae evolvuntur

deep.reconstruction: Problem V treats an Euler–Bernoulli beam of length a clamped at both ends. The modal shape is y = A cos Φ + B sin Φ + C e^Φ + D e^{-Φ}, with Φ = θx/b and ζ = θa/b. The conditions y = y' = 0 at x = 0 give A = −C − D and B = −C + D. The conditions at x = a (equations III and IV) are recombined as III·cos ζ − IV·sin ζ and III·sin ζ + IV·cos ζ, which gives two expressions for C/D. Setting them equal (page 482) and cross-multiplying, with s = sin ζ, c = cos ζ and E = e^ζ + e^{-ζ}, gives (s+c)E − 2 − 2sc = (s−c)E + 2 − 2sc. Hence cE = 2, that is cos ζ cosh ζ = 1. Euler notes this is the same frequency equation as in Problem I, the free–free beam, so the table of vibration periods and pitches is reused. Pitch is proportional to ζ²/π (times b²/a²) and the period is its reciprocal. The tabulated values are 7.1214, 19.6388, 40.1107, 63.5438. The Corollary remarks that clamped–clamped and free–free beams emit the same tones. Likewise, a beam pinned at one end has the same tones whether the other end is free or clamped (tan ζ = tanh ζ). Yet the cantilever (clamped–free) has different tones, cos ζ cosh ζ = −1, whose equation differs from the clamped–clamped and free–free one only in sign. Euler calls this a striking affinity but gives no explanation. The modern explanation is a boundary-condition duality. If w'''' = k⁴w is a free–free mode, then u = w'' satisfies the same equation and is a clamped–clamped mode, because u = w'' = 0 and u' = w''' = 0 at the ends. Pinned conditions (w = w'' = 0) map to pinned conditions under the same substitution, which explains the pinned–free / pinned–clamped coincidence. The cantilever maps to itself with its ends reversed. The only exception is the free–free rigid-body modes (ζ = 0, w'' ≡ 0), which have no clamped counterpart; this is the 'essential' difference that remains.
errors: The frequency equation cos ζ cosh ζ = 1 is derived correctly.

The third table entry is wrong. The roots are ζ ≈ 4.7300, 7.8532, 10.9956, 14.1372, so ζ²/π ≈ 7.1216, 19.631, 38.485, 63.62. Euler's 40.1107 (period 0.02493) corresponds to ζ ≈ 11.225 instead of 10.996; the correct values are about 38.49 and 0.02598.
The second and fourth entries are slightly off: 19.6388 vs 19.631, and 63.5438 vs 63.62.
Because the table is copied from Problem I, the same errors are presumably already present there.
The corollary does not mention that the free–free beam also has zero-frequency rigid-body motions, which the clamped–clamped beam lacks.

ideas.what: Frequency equation cos ζ cosh ζ = 1 for the clamped–clamped beam
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (E443, with Daniel Bernoulli's earlier work on beams)

ideas.what: Observation that clamped–clamped and free–free beams (and pinned–free / pinned–clamped beams) share their spectra, while the cantilever's equation differs only by a sign
ideas.modern_name: Spectral equivalence of dual boundary conditions under w ↦ w''
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler for the observation; the duality explanation belongs to later standard beam-vibration theory (e.g. Rayleigh-era treatments)

missed.claim: Euler notes the 'affinitas insignis' between boundary conditions but leaves it unexplained. The explanation, the w ↦ w'' duality that maps free conditions to clamped and pinned to pinned, is standard today, so this is not genuinely new.
missed.quote: affinitas certe insignis intercedit ratione formularum ex quibus angulum ζ elici oportet, quippe quae pro his casibus tantum signo differant
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Only of historical interest: it marks an early recognition of what later became the theory of dual or adjoint boundary conditions for fourth-order operators.

missed.claim: There is a numerical error in the third overtone (40.1107 should be about 38.49), presumably inherited from Problem I. Whether this is recorded in the Opera omnia commentary is unsure.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A minor historical correction to Euler's tables.

deep.surprise_reason: The result and the observation are known and credited to Euler; the duality explanation is standard. The only small finding is an apparently unremarked tabulation error in the third mode.
transcription_corrections: The image shows 'cof.' / 'fin.' (long s) where the transcription has cos./sin.; this is a modernization, not an error.
